Note any changes on the main lifts. Tap Show pictures or Show description on a move to see how it's done.
How to run it
Straight sets: do all the sets of each exercise, rest, then move to the next.
Main Circuit
Box squat – goblet
3 sets8-10 repsAny kit/Box~2kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand in front of a box at about parallel height holding a weight at the chest, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.

Movement: Sit the hips back and down to lightly touch the box, then drive up through the heels to stand tall, keeping the weight at the chest.

Focus: Keep the knees in line with the middle toes and the heels down. Touch the box under control rather than dropping, and keep the chest up and the weight close throughout.

Terminal knee extension
3 sets10 each sideBandLight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand with a band around the back of one knee anchored in front, a slight bend in that knee, holding a support.

Movement: Straighten the knee fully against the band, squeezing the thigh, then let it bend slightly under control.

Focus: Focus on fully straightening the knee and squeezing the front of the thigh hard at the top. Keep it slow and controlled, stay tall, and keep the movement pain-free.

Lat pulldown – wide grip
3 sets10 repsLat pulldown machineModerate
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Sit at the machine, thighs under the pads, a wide grip on the bar, arms extended, chest up.

Movement: Pull the bar down towards the upper chest, driving the elbows down and out, then return slowly under control.

Focus: Lead with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades down, not shrugging up towards the ears. Keep the chest up, don't lean back, and pull only to a comfortable shoulder range.

Seated cable row – single arm
3 sets10 each sideCable row machineModerate
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Sit at the low cable, a single handle in one hand, feet braced, arm extended, chest up, back tall.

Movement: Pull the handle to the side of the abdomen, driving the elbow back, then return slowly under control.

Focus: Lead with the elbow and squeeze the shoulder blade, keeping the torso square rather than rotating to pull. Keep the back tall and the shoulder down.

Calf raises – bilateral
3 sets10 repsStepBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand tall, feet hip-width, balls of the feet on the floor or the edge of a step, holding a support for balance.

Movement: Rise up onto the toes as high as you comfortably can, then lower the heels slowly under control.

Focus: Rise and lower slowly and evenly, not bouncing, through the full comfortable range. Keep the ankles tracking straight, not rolling out, and control the lower.

Balance – single leg knee drive
3 sets30s each sideKB/DBLight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand on one leg, torso tall, the other knee ready to drive up, arms ready.

Movement: Drive the free knee up towards hip height, hold the balance briefly, then lower under control and repeat.

Focus: Keep the hips level and the standing knee soft, staying tall as the knee drives up. Fix the eyes on a point, control the drive and lower, and keep the core engaged.

Straight arm pull-down – cable
3 sets10 repsCable machine~15kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand facing a high cable, arms extended up and forward on the bar, chest up, ribs down, core braced.

Movement: With straight arms, pull the bar down towards the thighs in an arc, then return slowly under control.

Focus: Keep the arms straight and drive from the lats, not bending the elbows. Keep the ribs down, don't lean back to help, and control the return.

Note any changes on the main lifts. Tap a move for cues.
How to run it
Straight sets: do all the sets of each exercise, rest, then move to the next.
Main Circuit
Romanian deadlift
3 sets8-10 repsAny kit~6kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand tall, feet hip-width, holding a weight in front of your thighs, or hands empty, with a soft bend in the knees. Set the shoulders back and brace the core.

Movement: Push the hips back and slide the weight down the front of your legs, keeping it close, until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings. Drive the hips forward to stand tall.

Focus: Keep the back flat throughout, never let it round. The movement is a hip hinge, not a squat, and the weight stays close to your legs. Only go as low as you can keep the back flat.

Meadows row
2 sets8-10 repsBarbell/LandmineModerate
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand side-on to a landmine bar, hinge with a flat back, one hand on the bar end, core braced.

Movement: Pull the bar towards the hip, driving the elbow back and up, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep the back flat and the hips still, leading with the elbow and squeezing the shoulder blade. Don't round or twist the torso to lift, and control the lower.

Suitcase carry
3 sets20mAny kitModerate
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand tall with a weight in one hand at the side like a suitcase, feet hip-width, ribs down, core braced.

Movement: Walk forward with controlled steps for the set distance, keeping the torso upright and level.

Focus: Resist the pull towards the weighted side, keeping the shoulders and hips level and the ribs down. Take steady steps, brace hard, and don't let the weight swing.

Resisted rotation – TRX
3 sets10-12 each sideTRXBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Hold the TRX handles together in front, arms extended, body leaning back slightly, feet planted, core braced.

Movement: Rotate the torso to one side, resisting the pull, then return and repeat to the other side.

Focus: Turn through the trunk and resist the strap's pull, keeping the arms fairly fixed. Keep the ribs down and the hips square, and control both directions.

Lateral raise – slow eccentric
2 sets8-10 each sideDBLight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand tall, a light dumbbell in each hand at the sides, elbows softly bent, ribs down.

Movement: Raise the arms out to shoulder height, then lower slowly over three to four seconds under control.

Focus: Lead with the elbows and keep the shoulders down, not shrugging, then control the slow lower. Use a light weight, and raise only to shoulder height.

Soleus – isometric hold
3 sets30sChairBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Sit on a chair, feet flat, knees bent to about a right angle. Everything above the ankles relaxed.

Movement: Press the balls of the feet down, lift the heels and hold at about half effort. Build into the hold, and lower under control.

Focus: The gentlest way to load the deep calf, and it suits an ankle that is still being careful. No impact, so it can be done often. Little and often rather than hard.

Single leg deadlift – bodyweight
3 sets10-12 each sideBodyweightBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand on one leg, torso tall, the other leg ready to travel back, standing knee soft, arms ready.

Movement: Hinge forward from the hip, letting the free leg travel back and the arms lower, then return to standing.

Focus: Hinge from the hip with a flat back, keeping the hips level and not opening out. Keep the standing knee soft, move slowly, and control the return.

Shoulder series – TRX
2 sets8-10 repsTRXBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Face the anchor, handles in hand, arms extended, body leaning back in a straight line, core braced.

Movement: Move through the set shoulder raises (Y, T and W positions) in sequence, squeezing the shoulder blades on each, controlled.

Focus: Keep the shoulders down through each position, not shrugging, and the body in a straight line. Squeeze the shoulder blades, and control each raise.

w/c 2 Nov 2026 · Squat & Hinge & Push▼
Goblet squat – pulse

Start: Hold a weight at the chest, elbows tucked, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.

Movement: Squat to a comfortable depth and pulse up and down through a small range at the bottom for the set count, then stand tall.

Focus: Keep the knees in line with the middle toes and the heels down through every pulse. Keep the chest up and the weight close, and pulse only within a depth the knees tolerate.

2 x 8-10 · Moderate
Romanian deadlift – staggered stance

Start: One foot flat, the other half a step back on its toes. Weight in front of the thighs, soft bend in the front knee.

Movement: Push the hips back and slide the weight down the front leg until the hamstring loads, then drive the hips forward to stand tall. Swap legs halfway.

Focus: Most of the weight sits on the front leg, the back foot is only there for balance. Back flat, hips square, not twisting open.

3 x 10-12 · 5kg
Bench press – narrow grip

Start: Lie on the bench, feet planted, shoulder blades pinched back and down, hands about shoulder-width, unrack over the chest.

Movement: Lower the bar under control to the lower chest, elbows tucked close to the body, then press back up to straight arms.

Focus: Keep the elbows tucked close, which brings in the triceps and eases the shoulders, and the shoulder blades set. Keep the wrists stacked, lower under control, and don't let the elbows flare.

2 x 8-10 · 2 x 4kg
Standing external rotation – arm raised

Start: Stand tall with the upper arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent to 90 degrees, forearm pointing forward, holding a light weight.

Movement: Rotate the forearm up towards the ceiling, keeping the upper arm parallel to the floor, then lower under control to the start.

Focus: Keep the upper arm still and level at shoulder height, and move only the forearm. Go very light, keep the shoulder down away from the ear, and stop short of anything that pinches at the top.

2 x 8-10 · 1.5kg
Rotator cuff – standing external rotation

Start: Stand tall holding a light dumbbell, the working elbow pinned to the ribs and bent to 90 degrees, forearm across the body.

Movement: Rotate the forearm outward away from the body, keeping the elbow pinned, then lower back across under control.

Focus: Keep the elbow glued to the side and move only the forearm. Keep the shoulder down and the ribs still, and take the speed out of it so the work stays in the cuff rather than the swing of the weight.

3 x 10 · 1.5kg
Leg extension – light and high rep

Start: Sit at the machine with a light weight, shins behind the pad, thighs supported, holding the handles.

Movement: Straighten the knees to raise the pad, then lower under control, for higher repetitions.

Focus: Keep the weight light and every rep smooth and controlled, never kicking. Keep the range comfortable and pain-free, building the thigh without stressing the knee.

2 x 8-10 · 8.25kg
Lateral band walks – diagonal

Start: Stand with a band around the legs, feet hip-width, knees softly bent, slight squat, torso tall.

Movement: Step diagonally forward and outward alternately, keeping tension on the band, for the set steps.

Focus: Keep tension on the band and the knees driving out, not caving. Stay low and controlled, and feel the outer hips working each step.

3 x 10-12 · Light
Halo – ViPR

Start: Stand tall holding the ViPR horizontally in both hands in front of the chest, feet hip-width, core braced.

Movement: Take the ViPR around the head in a controlled circle, one direction then the other, keeping the trunk stable.

Focus: Circle the ViPR around the head keeping the ribs down and the hips still, so the movement comes from the shoulders and upper back, not the lower back. Keep the circle smooth and the neck relaxed.

2 x 8-10 · Moderate
Side plank – feet stacked

Start: Lie on your side, forearm down with the elbow under the shoulder, legs straight and feet stacked.

Movement: Lift the hips so the body forms a straight line from head to heels and hold for the set time.

Focus: Keep the hips high and the body in one straight line, resisting the sag towards the floor. Keep the shoulder stacked over the elbow and the neck long, and stop when the line drops.

3 x 30s each side · Bodyweight

w/c 26 Oct 2026 · Squat & Hinge & Push▼
Suitcase squat

Start: Stand tall with a weight in one hand at the side like a suitcase, feet hip-width, ribs down, core braced.

Movement: Squat down by sending the hips back and bending the knees, then stand back up, keeping the torso upright.

Focus: Resist leaning towards the weight, keeping the shoulders and hips level and the ribs down. Keep the knees tracking over the feet, and stand tall throughout.

2 x 8-10 each side · Moderate
Good mornings – hugged

Start: Stand tall, feet hip-width, knees soft, hugging a weight to your chest with both arms, core braced.

Movement: Push the hips back and hinge forward with a flat back until the hamstrings load, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.

Focus: The weight sits high on the chest, so the back works hard to stay flat. Hinge at the hips, not the waist, and only go as far as that flat back allows.

3 x 10-12 · Moderate
Overhead press – around the clock, single arm

Start: Stand tall, a light weight at one shoulder, ribs down, core braced.

Movement: Press the weight overhead and move it through small controlled positions (front, side, angles) as set, keeping the arm working, then return.

Focus: Keep the ribs down and the core braced so the back doesn't arch as the arm moves. Keep the shoulder down, move slowly and controlled, and use a light weight given the changing angles.

2 x 8-10 each side · Light
Full can exercise

Start: Stand tall, arms down and slightly out in front at about 30 degrees, thumbs pointing up, light or no weight.

Movement: Raise the arms to shoulder height in that line with thumbs up, then lower under control.

Focus: Lead with the thumbs and keep the shoulders down, not shrugging, raising only to shoulder height. Use a light weight, and control the lower.

2 x 8-10 · Light
Knee extension – cable

Start: Sit or stand with a cuff around one ankle attached to a low cable behind, the knee slightly bent.

Movement: Straighten the knee against the cable, squeezing the thigh, then let it bend back under control.

Focus: Straighten under control and squeeze the thigh, never kicking the knee straight. Keep the range comfortable and pain-free, and control the return.

2 x 8-10 · Moderate
Hip abduction – cable, side step

Start: Stand with a cuff or band low around one ankle attached to a side cable, feet together, torso tall.

Movement: Step the working leg out to the side against the resistance, then step it back under control.

Focus: Keep the torso tall and the hips level, stepping from the outer hip, not leaning. Keep the steps controlled, and the working knee soft.

3 x 10-12 · Moderate
Y raise – TRX

Start: Face the anchor, handles in hand, arms extended, body leaning back in a straight line, core braced.

Movement: Raise the arms up and out into a Y as you rise, squeezing the shoulder blades, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep the shoulders down as the arms go overhead, not shrugging, and the body in a straight line. Squeeze the shoulder blades, and control the lower.

2 x 8-10 · Bodyweight
Hand plank

Start: Hands on the floor directly under your shoulders, arms straight, legs extended back with the toes tucked under.

Movement: Lift the hips to form a straight line and hold that position for the set time, breathing steadily throughout.

Focus: Keep a straight line from head to heels, hips neither sagging nor piking, and the ribs down. Push the floor away through the hands so the shoulder blades stay set rather than sinking between them. Come down when the line breaks or you feel it in the lower back.

2 x 20s · Bodyweight

Box squat – goblet

Start: Stand in front of a box at about parallel height holding a weight at the chest, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.

Movement: Sit the hips back and down to lightly touch the box, then drive up through the heels to stand tall, keeping the weight at the chest.

Focus: Keep the knees tracking over the toes and the heels down. Touch the box under control rather than dropping, and keep the chest up and the weight close throughout.

2 x 8-10 · ~2kg
Swings – KB

Start: Stand with a kettlebell on the floor in front, feet hip-width, hinged with a flat back, core braced.

Movement: Hike the kettlebell back between the legs, then drive the hips forward to swing it up to about chest height, letting it swing back down into the next hinge.

Focus: Power the swing from a sharp hip drive, not the arms or lower back, keeping the back flat throughout. Snap the glutes at the top with the ribs down, and let the arms just guide the bell.

3 x 10-12 · Moderate
Chest press – single arm

Start: Lie on a bench, a weight in one hand at chest height, the other arm out for balance, shoulder blades set, core braced.

Movement: Press the weight up until the arm is nearly straight, then lower under control to a comfortable stretch.

Focus: Keep the shoulder blades set and resist the torso twisting towards the free side. Keep the elbow at about 45 degrees, not flared, and control the lower.

2 x 8-10 each side · Moderate
Balance – single leg free

Start: Stand on one leg without support, torso tall, other foot lifted, arms ready to help balance.

Movement: Hold the single-leg balance freely for the set time, then swap.

Focus: Keep the hips level and the standing knee soft, fixing the eyes on a point ahead. Make small ankle adjustments to stay steady, and keep the core engaged.

3 x 30s each side · Bodyweight
Face pull – band, seated

Start: Sit tall, a band anchored in front at head height, a handle in each hand, arms extended forward, ribs down.

Movement: Pull the band towards the face, drawing the hands to the sides of the head with the elbows high, then return under control.

Focus: Lead with the elbows high and squeeze the shoulder blades, not shrugging up. Keep the ribs down and the neck relaxed, and control the return.

2 x 8-10 · Light band
Seated leg extension – bodyweight

Start: Sit tall on a chair or bench, one leg hanging with the knee bent, hands resting for support.

Movement: Straighten the knee to raise the lower leg, squeezing the thigh, then lower under control.

Focus: Straighten under control and squeeze the thigh at the top, never kicking the knee. Keep the range comfortable and pain-free, and control the lower.

2 x 8-10 · Bodyweight
Elbow plank – arm reach

Start: Set up in a forearm plank, straight line from head to heels, core and glutes braced.

Movement: Keeping the hips level, reach one arm forward off the floor, hold briefly, return, then the other.

Focus: Keep the hips level and square as you reach, resisting any twist. Keep the ribs down and the core braced, and keep the reach controlled so the line stays straight.

3 x 30s · Bodyweight
Glute bridge – single leg

Start: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg extended straight out and held off the floor.

Movement: Drive through the heel of the bent leg to push your hips up until the body is level. Hold two seconds, then lower slowly under control.

Focus: Keep the hips level, don't let the free side drop or twist. Push with the glute, not the lower back, and keep the ribs down.

3 x 10-12 each side · Bodyweight

Pull-through – cable

Start: Face away from a low cable, rope between your legs, feet shoulder-width. Step forward to take the tension, hands holding the rope, soft knees.

Movement: Push the hips back and let the rope draw between your legs with a flat back, then drive the hips forward to stand tall and squeeze the glutes.

Focus: Drive the movement from the hips, not the arms, the arms just hold the rope. Keep the back flat, and finish standing tall without leaning back or arching.

3 x 10 · 9.75kg
Meadows row

Start: Stand side-on to a landmine bar, hinge with a flat back, one hand on the bar end, core braced.

Movement: Pull the bar towards the hip, driving the elbow back and up, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep the back flat and the hips still, leading with the elbow and squeezing the shoulder blade. Don't round or twist the torso to lift, and control the lower.

2 x 8-10 · Moderate
Suitcase carry

Start: Stand tall with a weight in one hand at the side like a suitcase, feet hip-width, ribs down, core braced.

Movement: Walk forward with controlled steps for the set distance, keeping the torso upright and level.

Focus: Resist the pull towards the weighted side, keeping the shoulders and hips level and the ribs down. Take steady steps, brace hard, and don't let the weight swing.

3 x 20m · Moderate
Anterior tibialis – toe raises off a step

Start: Stand on a step or box with the heels on the surface and the toes hanging out over the edge. Hold a rail or frame for balance.

Movement: Let the toes lower below the level of the step under control, then pull them up towards the shins as high as they will go.

Focus: This is about range, not load. The edge lets the foot drop below level, which is where the shin has to work hardest and where most people have never trained. Go as low as the ankle allows before pulling back up, and keep the knees straight throughout.

3 x 10-12 · Bodyweight
Balance – single leg with arm reach

Start: Stand on one leg, torso tall, other foot lifted, arms ready to reach.

Movement: Reach the arms (and torso if set) out to the sides or forward, challenging balance, then return to centre.

Focus: Keep the hips level and the standing knee soft as you reach, moving slowly. Fix the eyes on a point, keep the core engaged, and return under control.

3 x 30s each side · Bodyweight
Straight arm pull-down – cable

Start: Stand facing a high cable, arms extended up and forward on the bar, chest up, ribs down, core braced.

Movement: With straight arms, pull the bar down towards the thighs in an arc, then return slowly under control.

Focus: Keep the arms straight and drive from the lats, not bending the elbows. Keep the ribs down, don't lean back to help, and control the return.

3 x 10 · 15.25kg
External rotation – band

Start: Stand side-on to a band at elbow height, elbow pinned to the side and bent to 90 degrees, forearm across the body.

Movement: Rotate the forearm outward, opening away from the body, keeping the elbow pinned, then return under control.

Focus: Keep the elbow glued to the side and move only the forearm, not the whole arm. Keep the shoulder down and the ribs still, and control the return.

2 x 8-10 each side · Light band
Elbow plank – leg lift

Start: Set up in a forearm plank, straight line from head to heels, core braced.

Movement: Keeping the hips level, lift one foot a few centimetres off the floor, hold briefly, lower, then the other.

Focus: Keep the hips level and square as the leg lifts, no rotating or sagging. Keep the ribs down and the core braced, and keep the lift small so the back stays neutral.

3 x 30s · Bodyweight

Bench press – narrow grip

Movement: Lower the bar under control to the lower chest, elbows tucked close to the body, then press back up to straight arms.

Single leg wall slide

Movement: Slide the arms slowly up the wall towards straight, keeping contact the whole way, then back down, balance held throughout.

Focus: The arms do the work, the standing leg is the challenge. Back, arms and hands stay on the wall, ribs down, hips level. Feel the balance in the standing foot and ankle.

ISO single leg deadlift – supported

Movement: Hinge at the hip and lower the weight down the standing leg while the free leg lifts behind, reach a flat-backed stretch, then hold still.

Focus: Back flat, hips level, don't let the raised hip open out. Light fingertip support only, enough to steady you, and take the hand away when you feel steady.

Internal rotation – cable

Start: Stand side-on to a cable at elbow height, the near elbow pinned to the side and bent to 90 degrees, forearm out to the side.

Movement: Rotate the forearm inward across the body, keeping the elbow pinned, then return under control.

Focus: Keep the elbow glued to the side and move only the forearm. Keep the shoulder down and the ribs still, and control the return.

2 x 8-10 · Light
Side plank – knees bent

Start: Lie on your side, forearm on the floor with the elbow under the shoulder, knees bent and stacked, hips off the floor.

Movement: Lift the hips so the body makes a straight line from head to knees and hold for the set time.

Focus: Keep the hips lifted and the body in a straight line, not letting the hips sag towards the floor. Keep the shoulder stacked over the elbow, and come down when the hips start to drop.

3 x 30s each side · Bodyweight

Leg press – wide stance

Start: Sit in the leg press, feet wide on the platform with the toes turned out, hips and back into the pad, core braced.

Movement: Lower under control to a comfortable depth, then press back up without locking out hard. The wide stance brings in the inner thigh and glutes.

Focus: Keep the knees tracking out over the toes in line with the turned-out feet, never caving in. Keep the hips flat and control the depth to what feels comfortable.

McGill curl-up – basic

Start: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg straight, hands under the lower back, elbows down.

Movement: Lift the head and shoulders just slightly off the floor, keeping the neck neutral, hold briefly, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep the lower back in its natural arch and lift only slightly, bracing the core rather than crunching. Keep the neck neutral and don't pull the chin to the chest.

2 x 6 each · Bodyweight
Balance board – double leg

Start: Stand on a balance board with both feet, knees soft, torso tall, near a support.

Movement: Keep the board level and steady, making constant small adjustments, for the set time.

Focus: Keep the knees soft and the hips level, adjusting from the ankles to keep the board steady. Fix the eyes on a point, keep the core engaged, and keep support within reach.

2 x 30s · Bodyweight
90/90 hip flow

Start: Sit on the floor with one leg bent in front at 90 degrees and the other out to the side at 90 degrees, sitting tall.

Movement: Flow the knees from side to side, rotating through both hips, pausing where you feel a gentle stretch, then continuing.

Focus: Move from the hips with the torso tall, easing into each side rather than forcing. Use the hands for support, and stay within a comfortable, pain-free range.

2 x 6 each way · Bodyweight
